title: Accounts Payable Clerk
description:

Client Details

A not-for-profit organisation based in Oxford.

Description
- Process invoices and ensure accurate data entry into the accounting system.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve any discrepancies promptly.
- Prepare and process payment runs in a timely manner.
- Maintain accurate records of all accounts payable transactions.
- Communicate effectively with suppliers to address and resolve queries.
- Assist with month-end closing activities related to accounts payable.
- Support the team with ad hoc finance-related tasks as required.
- Ensure compliance with organisational policies and procedures.

- Previous experience in accounts payable or a similar role in accounting and finance.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in processing financial data.
- Proficiency in using accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
- Good communication skills for liaising with suppliers and internal teams.
- A proactive and organised approach to managing tasks and meeting deadlines.

- Hourly rate of £13.00-£18.00, dependent on the level of experience.
- Temporary contract with the opportunity to make a valuable contribution to a not-for-profit organisation.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
A Bookkeeper role focusing on maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring smooth day to day financial operations. This position is key to supporting the accounting processes and helping the business stay on top of its finances.

Client Details

This organisation prides itself on it's collaboration and reputation in it's industry.

Description

The Bookkeeper's responsibilities include:
- Take ownership of the day-to-day finance operations, ensuring accurate and timely bookkeeping across the business.
- Manage the purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash processes, including invoice processing, payment runs, and credit control.
- Maintain accurate financial records through regular bank, supplier, customer, and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Process journals and assist with month-end activities, including accruals, prepayments, and ledger maintenance.
- Monitor cash flow and support effective cash management across the organisation.
- Assist with VAT submissions, audit requirements, and compliance-related finance activities.
- Work closely with the Finance Director to improve processes, support reporting, and contribute to the smooth running of the finance function.

Profile

A successful Bookkeeper should have:
- Experience in bookkeeping or a related accounting role.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Proficiency with accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
- An eye for detail and a methodical approach to work.
- A good understanding of financial principles and practices.
- Effective communication skills for liaising with internal and external stakeholders.

Job Offer

Benefits include:
- A permanent role in a friendly team.
- Salary ranging from £31,000 to £35,000.
- Good benefits package.
- Hybrid working (3 days in the office)
- Part time hours are also on offer.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Finance & Office Assistant
description:
Position: Finance & Office Assistant

Location: Oxford (OX44)

Salary: Up to £35,000 per annum

Hours: Monday - Friday (full-time)

Experience: Finance Assistant, Accounts Assistant, Sage, Sage Payroll, Office Administration, Credit Control, Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger, Payroll

The Opportunity

Thompson & Terry Recruitment are delighted to be working with a successful and well-established business, just south of Oxford, who are looking to recruit a Finance & Office Assistant to join their team.

As Finance & Office Assistant, you will support the day-to-day running of the finance and administration functions within a small but busy business. Working closely with colleagues across the business, you will play an important role in supporting payroll, invoicing, supplier administration and general office activities.

The successful Finance & Office Assistant will assist with purchase and sales ledger administration, processing supplier invoices, supporting project costing activities, customer invoicing, credit control, payroll administration, bank reconciliations and record maintenance. In addition to finance responsibilities, the role will include wider office administration duties to support the smooth running of the business.

This opportunity would suit a well-organised candidate who is looking to develop their experience within an SME environment. The successful Finance & Office Assistant will have strong attention to detail, good communication skills and a proactive approach.

The Company

Thompson & Terry Recruitment are proud to be working with a well-established Oxfordshire-based business with a strong reputation within its sector and a track record of delivering specialist projects for a diverse client base.

Operating within a busy and collaborative environment, the business works closely with customers, suppliers and project teams, creating a varied and engaging finance role with broad responsibilities across the organisation.

This position offers the opportunity to gain exposure to a varied finance and administration function while becoming part of a collaborative and supportive team environment.

Requirements
- Minimum 3 years' experience within a finance, accounts or office administration environment
- Relevant finance qualification, with experience using Sage
- Strong communication skills with excellent attention to detail
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple deadlines
- Experience within an SME environment, with a small business mentality

title: Finance Administrator
company: UCCF The Christian Unions - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are looking for a Finance Administrator to join our friendly Finance team and help ensure the smooth running of our purchase ledger and income processing functions.

This is an important role within the team, supporting the Finance team and colleagues across the organisation by providing accurate, timely and high quality financial administration.

The successful candidate will have experience of purchase ledger processing, working with payment providers and managing financial transactions. They will be highly organised, possess excellent communication skills and be comfortable managing a varied workload. Previous experience within a charity environment would be an advantage, although it is not essential.

The role

A significant part of the role will involve managing the purchase ledger, ensuring invoices and payments are processed accurately and in line with UCCF's financial policies and procedures. You will be responsible for helping to coordinate payment runs, ensuring suppliers are paid in a timely, efficient and cost effective manner.

You will also support our income processing activities, working closely with the Senior Finance Administrator to:
- Create and maintain donor records
- Process donations and other income accurately and efficiently
- Administer Gift Aid records and supporting documentation
- Undertake banking activities, including trips to the bank when required
- Support the reconciliation and recording of income transactions

About you

You will be:
- Accurate and methodical, with excellent attention to detail.
- Comfortable working with financial systems and databases.
- Able to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- A strong communicator with excellent customer service skills.
- Committed to maintaining confidentiality and handling sensitive information appropriately.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with both financial data and people, and wants to contribute to the work of a Christian charity that supports students across the UK.

If you are looking for a varied finance role within a supportive team environment, we'd love to hear from you.

The details

Salary: £27,175 - £31,601 depending on experience

Hours: Full-time of 37.5 hours per week. We are also open to discussing part time.

Holiday: 30 days holiday per year, plus 8 public holidays

Location: Hybrid working from our Oxford office

Interview date: Thursday 29 October

Our benefits
- 30 days annual leave, plus public holidays
- 5 days of service leave
- Modern and spacious central Oxford office
- Facilities including secure bike storage
- Cycle to work scheme
- Free access to counselling and healthcare support, including discounted gym memberships
- Generous enhanced family leave and pay provision

To apply

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
We are recruiting for a leading company dedicated to delivering high-quality research solutions. We are now looking for a meticulous and organised Part-Time Payroll Administrator the team on a 12 month FTC

The Role

In this position, you will take ownership of our end-to-end payroll processing for up to 16 hours a week. You will ensure our dedicated laboratory and administrative staff are paid accurately and on time, while maintaining full compliance with statutory regulations.

Key Responsibilities
- Payroll Processing: Manage the end-to-end processing of monthly payroll for all salaried and hourly contracted laboratory staff.
- Data Management: Calculate and input overtime, shift allowances, sickness (SSP), maternity/paternity pay, and unpaid leave.
- Pensions & Benefits: Administer workplace pension contributions and student loan deductions.
- Compliance & Reporting: Submit accurate RTI data to HMRC and process year-end requirements (P60s, P45s).
- Queries: Act as the first point of contact for staff payroll queries, resolving them efficiently and discreetly.

What We Are Looking For
- Proven experience as a Payroll Administrator or in a similar finance/HR administration role.
- Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation, HMRC regulations, and auto-enrolment pensions.
- Exceptional attention to detail and a high level of confidentiality.
- Excellent communication skills

What We Offer
- Highly flexible working hours spread across 2-4 days to suit your schedule.
- Pro-rata annual leave and company pension scheme.
- A supportive, modern work environment within a cutting-edge industry.
- Free on-site parking and access to employee well-being programmes.
